title: Passive Voice Quiz 4
description: Turn active sentences into the passive, and make passive negatives and questions.
topic: Active to passive, negatives and questions
instructions: Passive Voice: Active to passive, negatives and questions.
Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Which sentence is the passive of 'She saw him'?
questions.explanation: The object him becomes the subject he, and the doer becomes an object pronoun after by. Watch out: him cannot be a subject.

questions.question: Make the negative: 'The letter was sent.'
questions.explanation: The negative adds not after the first helper: wasn't sent. Watch out: did is never added in the passive.

questions.question: {{1}} the room {{2}} (clean) yet? Use the present perfect passive.
questions.explanation: The question puts Has in front of the subject, and been cleaned stays after it. Watch out: only the first helper moves.

questions.question: When {{1}} the window {{2}} (break)?
questions.explanation: Past simple passive question: When + was + subject + participle. Watch out: the participle of break is broken.

questions.question: In 'Hamlet was written by Shakespeare', the by-phrase can be dropped without losing information.
questions.explanation: The doer is the important new information here, so by Shakespeare stays. Watch out: the by-phrase is dropped only when the doer is unknown or unimportant.

questions.question: Which question is correct?
questions.explanation: Was goes in front of the subject, and the participle follows. Watch out: did is not used, and the participle cannot be the base form.

questions.question: Choose the passive verb group.

rows.given: The chef cooks the meal. The meal ___ by the chef.
Anna is painting the wall. The wall ___ by Anna.
Someone has stolen my phone. My phone ___.
They will open the shop. The shop ___.
Workers built the bridge. The bridge ___ by workers.

questions.explanation: Keep the tense of the active verb. Watch out: the continuous needs being and the perfect needs been.

questions.question: Match each active sentence with its passive.
questions.explanation: The tense stays the same, and be carries it. Watch out: is cleaning becomes is being cleaned, and has cleaned becomes has been cleaned.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order to make a question.
questions.explanation: The question word comes first, then was, then the subject, then the participle. Watch out: was moves in front of the subject.

questions.question: Which sentences are correct?
options: The window wasn't broken by me.
questions.explanation: The correct sentences keep the helper before the subject in questions, or add not after the helper. Watch out: didn't and did cannot be used with a passive verb.

questions.question: Why is the doer left out in 'My bag was stolen'?
questions.explanation: The thief is unknown, so there is nothing to put after by. Watch out: the verb being irregular or negative has nothing to do with it.

questions.question: Turn into the passive: 'They cancelled the match.'
accepted: The match was cancelled by them.
The match was cancelled by them
questions.explanation: The object the match becomes the subject, and cancelled becomes was cancelled. Watch out: the tense stays the past simple, so it is was, not has been.
